decisions.executionNote: Approach the metal compass with the left arm, beginning a gradual downward wrist orientation while keeping clearance. Right arm remains still.
The initial approach was rejected without motion. Retry with much smaller position and orientation increments to preserve joint continuity.
Continue the left-arm approach above the compass, gradually pitching the open gripper downward with small continuous joint changes.
Advance toward the compass from the left workspace while increasing the downward pitch; keep the gripper open and above the surrounding objects.
Move the open left gripper farther forward above the target and continue rotating toward a vertical grasp, without crossing the center workspace.
Bring the left gripper over the compass while finishing most of the downward orientation. Maintain height until alignment can be checked visually.
Replan from the executed prefix using smaller increments after the continuity guard. Approach a centered top-down grasp of the compass.
Finish the downward wrist pitch and move over the upper portion of the compass. Begin a shallow descent while leaving the jaws open.
Use smaller increments after the interrupted approach. Set the gripper nearly vertical and lower slowly over the compass's upper legs.
Lower the vertical open jaws toward the compass, with a small forward correction to favor the hinge and upper legs. Check contact height before closing.
Descent showed a significant residual, so stop pushing downward. Make a small lateral centering correction and close around the compass; retention must be checked on lifting.
Keep the jaws commanded fully closed, allow the closure to settle, then begin a small test lift to verify that the compass follows the gripper.
The compass appears retained during the test lift. Continue lifting with the gripper closed and a slight backward motion to preserve reach margin and elbow configuration.
The compass stays fixed between the jaws in the wrist view. Lift another six centimeters with slight retraction, keeping the gripper closed to exceed the requested ten-centimeter elevation.
